t: LeetCode 2067 - Number of Equal Count Substrings: One Window Width per Letter Total
o: **Understanding the problem.** A substring is an equal-count substring when every distinct letter it contains occurs exactly count times; letters absent from it are irrelevant. For s = "aaabcbbcc" with count = 3 the qualifiers are "aaa" (indices 0-2), "bcbbcc" (3-8) and the full string - three in total. With s = "abcd" and count = 2 no letter even reaches multiplicity 2 anywhere in s, so the answer is 0. The structural lever: a qualifying substring spanning u distinct letters must have length exactly u * count, and since the alphabet has 26 letters only 26 candidate window widths exist, each verifiable with a linear fixed-size slide.
k: A valid substring with u distinct letters has length exactly u * count - at most 26 widths to consider.
While sliding a fixed window, validity is equivalent to the number of letters whose frequency equals count being exactly u; those frequencies then fill the window completely.
A matched counter updated on crossings of the value count keeps each slide step O(1).

a.i: Extend a substring from every start while maintaining letter frequencies plus two counters: distinct (letters present) and matched (letters at exactly count). Equality of the counters certifies validity, and growth aborts as soon as any letter exceeds count.
s: For each start, clear a 26-slot table and set distinct = matched = 0.
Extend the end one character at a time, updating frequency, distinct, and matched.
Stop extending when some letter frequency surpasses count.
Add one to the answer whenever matched == distinct.
a.t: O(n^2) worst case - extensions can run long when count dwarfs letter supplies

a.n: Approach 2: Fixed Windows for Every u
a.i: Enumerate u from 1 to 26 and slide a window of width u * count. Track matched, the number of letters occurring exactly count times. Because window frequencies sum to the width, matched == u forces every letter present to appear exactly count times - no other checks are needed.
s: For each u from 1 to 26 set the width w = u * count; abandon u once w exceeds n.
Sweep i across s, absorbing s[i] and expelling s[i - w] to keep the window exactly w wide.
Move matched up or down whenever a frequency crosses the boundary at count in either direction.
Once i reaches w - 1, count the window whenever matched == u.
a.t: O(26 n) - 26 linear passes with O(1) updates per character

w: Open with the length identity u * count - it converts a vague counting task into 26 mechanical window slides. Pitfalls: matched must be maintained on BOTH crossings of count (reaching it and leaving it) for additions and removals alike, and remember to break early once u * count exceeds n. Follow-ups: a larger alphabet scales the outer loop linearly; variants like every letter appearing at most count times reuse the same machinery.
